Keywords: The

outputs.L1: A volatile memory device includes a refresh controller configured to control a hidden refresh operation performed on a first portion of memory cells while a valid operation is performed on a second portion of the memory cells. The volatile memory device is configured to perform a regular refresh operation in response to receiving a refresh command. The volatile memory device is configured to perform a desired number of regular refresh operations during a remaining part of the reference time based on the refresh information. outputs.L2: A volatile memory device has a refresh controller that manages a hidden refresh process carried out on one group of memory cells at the same time that a valid operation is executed on another group of memory cells. The device is designed to carry out a regular refresh process when it receives a refresh command. During an initial segment of a reference time, the refresh controller produces refresh information based on a performance indicator associated with the hidden refresh process. Using that refresh information, the volatile memory device performs a desired quantity of regular refresh processes during the remaining segment of the reference time. This desired quantity is an integer determined from the difference between a target number of refresh processes for the reference time and a count value representing hidden refresh processes during that reference time.
outputs.L3:
A volatile memory device may include a refresh controller configured to manage refresh activity for the memory cells of the device. In particular, the refresh controller may perform hidden refresh operations on one portion of the memory cells while valid memory operations, such as read or write operations, are being performed on another portion of the memory cells. In this manner, at least some refresh operations can be carried out in the background without interrupting normal access to other portions of the memory array.

The volatile memory device may also perform regular refresh operations in response to receiving refresh commands. These regular refresh operations may be externally commanded or otherwise initiated according to a refresh schedule, and may be used to ensure that memory cells retain their stored data within a required retention period.

During a first part of a reference time period, the refresh controller may monitor or evaluate hidden refresh operations and generate refresh information based on a performance indicator associated with those hidden refresh operations. The performance indicator may include, for example, a count of hidden refresh operations successfully performed during the first part of the reference time period, or other information indicating how much refresh progress has been achieved through hidden refresh activity.

Based on the generated refresh information, the volatile memory device may determine how many regular refresh operations should be performed during a remaining part of the reference time period. The device may then perform that desired number of regular refresh operations during the remaining part of the reference time, thereby compensating for any shortfall in hidden refresh activity and maintaining an overall required refresh rate.

The desired number of regular refresh operations may be determined by comparing a target refresh count for the reference time period with the number of hidden refresh operations performed during that same reference time period. In particular, the desired number may correspond to the difference between the target refresh count and the count of hidden refresh operations. As a result, when a greater number of hidden refresh operations have been completed, fewer regular refresh operations may be required, and when fewer hidden refresh operations have been completed, a greater number of regular refresh operations may be performed to satisfy the target refresh requirement.
outputs.L4:
A volatile memory device, such as a dynamic random-access memory device, includes a memory array divided into multiple portions and a refresh controller configured to manage refresh operations for the memory array. Because data stored in volatile memory cells can degrade over time, the memory device periodically performs refresh operations to preserve the stored data. The refresh controller is arranged to perform at least some of these refresh operations as hidden refresh operations. During a hidden refresh operation, one portion of the memory array is refreshed while another portion of the memory array remains available for normal, valid memory operations, such as read or write operations. In this manner, refresh activity can be performed in the background with reduced impact on externally visible memory access performance.

The refresh controller also monitors the execution of hidden refresh operations during at least a portion of a reference time period. Based on the number, rate, timing, or effectiveness of the hidden refresh operations completed during that portion of the reference time period, the controller generates refresh information indicating how much refresh work has already been performed. This refresh information may represent, for example, a count of hidden refresh operations, a remaining refresh requirement, or a difference between a target refresh count and the number of refresh operations already completed.

Using the generated refresh information, the memory device determines an adjusted number of regular refresh operations to be performed during another portion of the reference time period or during a subsequent refresh interval. The adjusted number is an integer number selected so that, when combined with the hidden refresh operations already performed, the total number of refresh operations satisfies or approaches a target refresh count for the reference time period. If many hidden refresh operations have been successfully completed, the number of regular refresh operations may be reduced. If fewer hidden refresh operations have been completed, the number of regular refresh operations may be increased to ensure that data retention requirements are still met.

By coordinating hidden refresh operations with regular refresh operations in this manner, the volatile memory device can maintain the required refresh coverage while reducing unnecessary refresh overhead. The approach improves refresh scheduling flexibility, helps preserve memory data integrity, and allows valid memory accesses to continue efficiently even while refresh maintenance is being performed.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article because it points to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when someone says “the book,” they are not talking about any book, but a particular book that the listener likely knows about.

Although “the” may seem simple, it helps make sentences clearer and more precise. It can turn a general noun into something specific: “a car” could mean any car, while “the car” refers to one certain car. This small word guides the reader or listener and adds meaning without drawing attention to itself.

In writing and speech, “the” appears so often that people rarely notice it. However, without it, English would sound incomplete and confusing. The word “the” shows that even the smallest words can have great importance in language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a volatile memory device that uses hidden refresh operations during valid memory operations and adjusts regular refresh commands based on a target refresh count over a reference time.
counterfactuals.output: A volatile memory device includes a memory cell array, refresh control circuitry, and command logic configured to perform hidden refresh operations during valid memory operations, such as read, write, activate, or precharge operations, without requiring a dedicated external refresh command. The refresh control circuitry maintains refresh-count information corresponding to hidden refresh operations performed within a reference time interval and compares the refresh-count information with a target refresh count for the reference time interval. Based on the comparison, the command logic adjusts execution of regular refresh commands, including selectively delaying, suppressing, shortening, or otherwise modifying regular refresh operations when hidden refresh operations satisfy at least a portion of the target refresh count. When the hidden refresh operations are insufficient to meet the target refresh count, regular refresh operations are executed to maintain data retention. The device thereby reduces refresh overhead, improves memory availability, and maintains required refresh coverage for volatile memory cells.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single-paragraph technical summary of an invention involving a refresh controller for DRAM that tracks hidden refresh performance and determines how many regular refresh operations remain to be performed in a reference interval.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a DRAM refresh controller that manages refresh scheduling by accounting for both regular refresh operations and “hidden” refresh operations performed opportunistically during memory idle periods or overlapping with other activity. The controller tracks hidden refresh performance over a defined reference interval and determines, from that tracking, how many required regular refresh operations remain to satisfy the DRAM refresh requirement for the interval. Based on this determination, the controller can adjust the issuance of subsequent regular refresh commands, reducing unnecessary refresh activity when sufficient hidden refreshes have already occurred while ensuring that all memory rows are refreshed within the mandated retention time. This approach improves memory availability and power efficiency by minimizing disruptive regular refresh cycles without compromising data integrity.

performing a hidden refresh operation on a second portion of the memory cell array during the accessing of the first portion, the second portion being different from the first portion;

compute a residual refresh quantity as a difference between a target refresh quantity and a counted number of the hidden refresh operations; and  
generate an integer regular refresh count from the residual refresh quantity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for a semiconductor memory patent where refresh information is generated from a performance indicator of hidden refresh operations during a first part of a reference time, and regular refresh operations are scheduled during the remaining part.
counterfactuals.output: A semiconductor memory device includes a memory cell array and refresh control circuitry configured to manage refresh operations within a reference time period. During a first portion of the reference time period, the refresh control circuitry performs hidden refresh operations and generates refresh information based on a performance indicator associated with the hidden refresh operations. The performance indicator may indicate, for example, a number, rate, completion state, or execution result of the hidden refresh operations. During a remaining portion of the reference time period, the refresh control circuitry schedules regular refresh operations based on the generated refresh information. By adjusting regular refresh scheduling according to refresh information derived from hidden refresh performance, the semiconductor memory device may improve refresh efficiency, reduce interference with normal access operations, and maintain data retention reliability.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following invention in formal patent language: a volatile memory refresh controller performs hidden refresh concurrently with valid operations, counts those hidden refreshes, receives refresh commands for regular refresh, and bases the desired number of regular refreshes on the gap between target and hidden refresh counts.
counterfactuals.output: A volatile memory refresh control apparatus is provided for managing refresh operations of a volatile memory device. The apparatus includes a refresh controller configured to perform hidden refresh operations concurrently with valid memory access operations, maintain a count of the hidden refresh operations performed, receive one or more refresh commands associated with regular refresh operations, and determine a desired number of regular refresh operations based at least in part on a difference between a target refresh count and the count of hidden refresh operations. The refresh controller thereby reduces or adjusts regular refresh activity in view of refresh operations already performed during valid operations while maintaining a required refresh rate for the volatile memory device.
